focus: Type inference, variable formation, control-flow structuring, emission, and the global edit-state-then-rerun-everything intervention model

pipeline.name: Initialization (ActionStart, ActionConstbase, ActionDefaultParams)
pipeline.description: Sets up initial state: register maps, constant identification, default function prototypes, and spacebase initialization. These run once per function to establish baseline data-flow facts.
pipeline.outputs: Initial Varnode types, spacebase references, basic prototype data

pipeline.name: Prototype Recovery Phase 1 (ActionPrototypeTypes, ActionFuncLink)
pipeline.description: Establishes initial function signatures and parameter/return types from known prototypes, call sites, and storage conventions. Links function symbols to call sites.
pipeline.inputs: Function symbols, architecture calling conventions, database prototypes
pipeline.outputs: Locked prototype data, formal parameter/return varnodes

pipeline.name: Full Loop (rule_repeatapply): Main Loop with Data-Flow Analysis (mainloop ActionGroup)
pipeline.description: Iteratively applies control-flow analysis (unreachable blocks, heritage, segment analysis), dead code removal, type inference, variable restructuring, and transformation rules. Repeats until no changes occur.
pipeline.inputs: Function data-flow graph, Varnode instances, PcodeOps, types, prototypes
pipeline.outputs: Refined data-flow graph, improved type information, merged variables, simplified operations

pipeline.name: Type Recovery Iteration 1-7 (ActionInferTypes within mainloop)
pipeline.description: Propagates data types across data-flow edges using lattice-based inference. buildLocaltypes() initializes types, propagateOneType() spreads types along uses/definitions, writeBack() commits changes. Repeats up to 7 times if types change, with restart mechanism.
pipeline.inputs: Current Varnode type assignments, PcodeOp type transfer rules (per-opcode)
pipeline.outputs: Updated Varnode types; if changed, sets restart flag for next mainloop iteration

pipeline.name: Dead Code and Alias Analysis (ActionDeadCode, ActionDynamicMapping)
pipeline.description: Identifies and removes unused operations, analyzes storage alias relationships, and sets up dynamic symbol tracking for ephemeral temporaries via DynamicHash.
pipeline.outputs: Dead ops removed, alias sets computed, dynamic symbol mappings

pipeline.name: Spacebase and Nonzero Mask Analysis (ActionSpacebase, ActionNonzeroMask)
pipeline.description: Establishes spacebase (stack pointer) tracking and computes nonzero bitmasks for values, enabling better pointer/array analysis.
pipeline.inputs: Data-flow for spacebase varnodes, arithmetic operations
pipeline.outputs: Spacebase reference graph, nonzero masks on varnodes

pipeline.name: Transformation Rules Pool (oppool1: 100+ rules applied repeatedly)
pipeline.description: Applies peephole optimization and data-flow simplification rules (e.g., algebraic identities, constant propagation, bit manipulation simplifications). Each rule checks applicability per operation.
pipeline.outputs: Simplified data-flow (fewer ops, more constants, better structure)

pipeline.name: Variable Merge Phase (ActionMergeRequired, ActionMergeAdjacent, ActionMergeMultiEntry, ActionMergeCopy)
pipeline.description: Combines multiple Varnode instances representing the same high-level variable at different control-flow points. Required merges (forced by semantics) vs speculative (heuristic-based) vs adjacent (contiguous storage).
pipeline.inputs: Varnodes with cover information, control-flow graph
pipeline.outputs: HighVariable instances with merged Varnodes, reduced variable count

pipeline.name: Explicit/Implied Marking (ActionMarkExplicit, ActionMarkImplied)
pipeline.description: Determines which Varnodes appear as explicit tokens in output vs are inlined into parent expressions. Heuristics based on usage count, type, and cover.
pipeline.inputs: HighVariables, Varnode usage counts, expression trees

pipeline.name: Variable Naming (ActionNameVars)
pipeline.description: Assigns user-readable names to HighVariables by consulting Symbol table, function parameters, and data-flow heuristics. Prefers mapped addresses and parameter names.

pipeline.name: Control-Flow Structuring (ActionBlockStructure via CollapseStructure)
pipeline.description: Transforms unstructured control-flow graph into nested block structures (if-then-else, while, for, switch). Rules applied in priority order; unstructurable edges marked as gotos. Runs twice: early (with transformations allowed) and late (analysis-only).
pipeline.inputs: CFG with unreachable edges marked, loop structure
pipeline.outputs: Structured block hierarchy (BlockIf, BlockWhile, BlockSwitch, BlockGoto)

pipeline.name: Cast Strategy (ActionSetCasts)
pipeline.description: Inserts explicit casts in output where type conversions occur, using language-specific rules (CastStrategyC). Determines minimum necessary cast set.
pipeline.inputs: HighVariables with final types, type transfer rules

pipeline.name: Final Structure and Cleanup (ActionFinalStructure, ActionStop)
pipeline.description: Last structuring pass on residual edges, final validation, and completion marker. Prepares for emission.
pipeline.outputs: Finalized control-flow structure ready for code printing

feedback_loops.name: Type Propagation Convergence Loop
feedback_loops.mechanism: localcount incremented; if localcount < 7 and types changed, action returns 0 (continue). ActionRestartGroup parent checks hasRestartPending(); if true, resets all sibling actions and re-runs the entire mainloop ActionGroup.

feedback_loops.name: Data-Flow Graph Restart from Prototype Changes
feedback_loops.trigger: ActionPrototypeTypes, ActionActiveReturn, or other prototype-modifying actions call data.setRestartPending(true)
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ActionStart of the next mainloop iteration
feedback_loops.mechanism: ActionRestartGroup::apply() detects restartPending flag, calls data.getArch()->clearAnalysis(), resets all actions in mainloop, then re-executes entire mainloop. Max 1 restart allowed at top level.

feedback_loops.name: Rule-Based Simplification Iteration
feedback_loops.trigger: Any Rule in oppool1 successfully applies (changes an operation)
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Beginning of oppool1 (rule pool repeats immediately)
feedback_loops.mechanism: ActionPool has rule_repeatapply flag; after each rule fires, if any rule applied in this pass, oppool1 loop continues. When no rule applies in a full pass, loop exits.

feedback_loops.name: Loop-Based Structuring Iteration
feedback_loops.trigger: CollapseStructure::collapseInternal() successfully applies any ruleBlock* pattern
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: collapseInternal() top (re-evaluates same block or moves to next)
feedback_loops.mechanism: ruleBlock* returns true when it restructures. collapseInternal() maintains a worklist of blocks to process; after each successful rule, graph may change, so loop reconsiders blocks. Inner loop continues until no more rules apply.

feedback_loops.name: Type Propagation Interaction with Prototype Refinement
feedback_loops.trigger: Type inference infers a more specific function signature (e.g., parameter types from call sites)
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ActionPrototypeTypes, which may call setRestartPending if prototype changed
feedback_loops.mechanism: Type inference results feed into prototype recovery; improved types may refine parameter descriptions, triggering prototype-level restart.

feedback_loops.name: Merge-Induced Cover Changes
feedback_loops.trigger: HighVariable::merge() combines varnodes; cover becomes union of member covers
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Type and symbol lookup for merged variable (updateType, updateSymbol called)
feedback_loops.mechanism: HighVariable dirty flags (coverdirty, typedirty, symboldirty) are set when merge occurs. Lazy re-computation on next access (updateCover(), updateType()).

feedback_loops.name: User Edit -> Full Recompilation Cycle
feedback_loops.trigger: User renames variable, locks/unlocks type, or changes override via Java GUI; database mutated; decompile() called again
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ActionStart (full decompilation restart with modified Symbol state)
feedback_loops.mechanism: Symbol flags (typelock, namelock) and override state persisted in database. Each decompile() call loads fresh symbol state and runs full action pipeline. Type locks prevent propagateTypeEdge from overwriting inferred type.
feedback_loops.anchor: database.hh:230-232 (isTypeLocked, isNameLocked), action.hh:298+ (ActionDatabase controls full pipeline re-entry)

feedback_loops.name: Alias-Based Type Refinement Loop
feedback_loops.trigger: Alias analysis discovers storage overlaps; type inference re-examines aliased values
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: Type inference propagation for affected varnodes
feedback_loops.mechanism: ActionDynamicMapping builds alias groups; union resolution may create new symbols. If union facet symbols created, dynamic hash entries attach to varnodes, affecting their type decisions on re-propagation.

feedback_loops.name: Dead Code Removal Triggering Variable Reassignment
feedback_loops.trigger: ActionDeadCode removes an operation; varnode outputs become disconnected
feedback_loops.rewinds_to: ActionAssignHigh (re-evaluates which varnodes map to which HighVariables)
feedback_loops.mechanism: When ops are removed, their output varnodes no longer have uses. HighVariable membership changes, triggering re-evaluation of variable boundaries and merges.

decision_points.name: Type Propagation Pass Limit (Empirical Threshold)
decision_points.decision: Stop type propagation after 7 iterations. Constant is hard-coded; when localcount >= 7, set warning flag and return 0.
decision_points.alternatives: Lower limits (e.g., 3-5) would speed up but risk incomplete type recovery. Higher limits (8+) might converge better on complex mutually-dependent types but risk infinite loops or excessive time.
decision_points.current_override: None user-facing; compile-time source change only

decision_points.name: Type Lattice Flow Direction per Opcode
decision_points.decision: Each opcode defines its own type transfer rules: which inputs/outputs propagate what types, transformations applied. Hard-coded per opcode class (e.g., TypeOpLoad::propagateType does input-pointer → output-value).
decision_points.alternatives: Bidirectional propagation would allow pointer type to refine load output but also output value to refine pointer (circular). One-directional preserves acyclicity but loses bidirectional constraints.

decision_points.name: Union Field Scoring Heuristics
decision_points.decision: Scores candidate union fields by size match, type compatibility, and data-flow frequency. Heuristics are hard-coded weights in the scoring logic.
decision_points.alternatives: Different weights favor different field candidates. Higher weight on size → prefer exact matches; higher on type → prefer semantic compatibility.

decision_points.name: Type Lock Enforcement at Propagation Boundary
decision_points.decision: If outvn->isTypeLock(), return false immediately (type locked varnodes block propagation). Type lock originates from Symbol::isTypeLocked() (user-locked) or Varnode::typelock flag.
decision_points.alternatives: If type locks are ignored, inferred types override user intent. If partial propagation allowed through locks (e.g., only for compatible supertypes), could preserve some constraints.
decision_points.current_override: Symbol type lock set via database/UI; user can lock/unlock types, preventing automatic changes

decision_points.name: Merge Strategy Selection (Forced vs Speculative vs Adjacent)
decision_points.decision: mergeTestRequired() forces merges when data-flow semantics demand it (phi functions). mergeTestSpeculative() uses heuristics (cover overlap, similar types). mergeTestAdjacent() merges contiguous storage. Each test has hard-coded conditions.
decision_points.alternatives: More conservative (only forced) preserves variable distinctions but increases count. More aggressive (always speculative) reduces count but may merge unrelated variables.
decision_points.current_override: Symbol::setIsolated(bool) prevents speculative merging of a specific variable

decision_points.name: Explicit vs Implied Varnode Decision (Output Readability Control)
decision_points.decision: baseExplicit() heuristic: if varnode has multiple uses or is in a control-flow sensitive context, mark explicit. checkImpliedCover() checks if variable can be safely inlined without violating cover constraints. Hard-coded heuristics.
decision_points.alternatives: More explicit = more tokens, clearer data-flow, more verbose. More implied = cleaner expressions, harder to trace execution.

decision_points.name: Control-Flow Rule Application Order (Structuring Precedence)
decision_points.decision: Try rules in hard-coded order: Goto, Cat (sequence), ProperIf, IfElse, WhileDo, DoWhile, InfLoop, Switch, then IfNoExit. First rule that matches applies; loop continues.
decision_points.alternatives: Different ordering would change which structures are preferred when multiple patterns match. E.g., if-then-else vs if-then-if-goto sequence, while vs for-loop vs if-based loop.

decision_points.name: Unstructured Edge Selection Heuristic (Goto Placement)
decision_points.decision: Rank unstructured edges by 'likelihood' (block reachability, frequency heuristics, entry/exit patterns). Mark most likely edge as goto. Likelihood computation is hard-coded.
decision_points.alternatives: Different heuristics (e.g., based on jump distance, block size, branch probability) would change which edges become gotos vs part of nested structure.

decision_points.name: Cast Emission Strategy (Type Conversion Display)
decision_points.decision: Determines when explicit casts appear in output. Checks type compatibility; if incompatible, insert cast. Logic is language-specific (C vs Java have different rules).
decision_points.alternatives: Always-cast = verbose but explicit; never-cast = clean but ambiguous. Heuristic-based balances both.
decision_points.current_override: OptionNoCastPrinting globally disables casts; otherwise heuristic

decision_points.name: NULL Pointer Keyword Printing
decision_points.decision: If option_NULL = true, print null pointers as 'NULL' keyword; else as '0'. Set by OptionNullPrinting option.
decision_points.alternatives: NULL is more semantic (source-like); 0 is more literal (closer to binary).

decision_points.name: Integer Constant Display Format
decision_points.decision: Global OptionIntegerFormat sets default (decimal, hex, octal, binary). Per-Symbol Symbol::displayFormat() overrides for equates and named constants.
decision_points.alternatives: Hex aids bit-pattern reasoning; decimal for arithmetic; octal/binary for specific domains.
decision_points.current_override: OptionIntegerFormat global option; Symbol::setDisplayFormat() per-symbol override

intervention_surfaces.name: Symbol Type Lock (typelock flag)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can lock a Symbol's data-type via the GUI. When set, type propagation is blocked from overwriting the type (propagateTypeEdge checks isTypeLock() and returns false). Prevents automatic type changes.

intervention_surfaces.name: Symbol Name Lock (namelock flag)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can lock a Symbol's name, preventing automatic renaming. Checked by ActionNameVars to preserve user-chosen names.

intervention_surfaces.name: Symbol Isolation Flag (isolate display flag)
intervention_surfaces.description: Symbol::setIsolated(true) prevents a variable from being speculatively merged with others. Preserves separate variable identity even if heuristics suggest merging.
intervention_surfaces.affects: Merge class mergeTestSpeculative checks symbol isolate flag

intervention_surfaces.name: Type Override (Symbol::overrideSizeLockType)
intervention_surfaces.description: Allows changing the data-type of a size-locked symbol while preserving the lock. Used when lock is on size only, not on the underlying type structure.

intervention_surfaces.name: Dynamic Symbol Facets (UnionFacetSymbol)
intervention_surfaces.description: User can create a UnionFacetSymbol pointing to a specific union field at a code address. Attaches to a temporary varnode via DynamicHash to override union field interpretation at that point.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionNullPrinting
intervention_surfaces.description: Boolean option: if on, print null pointers as 'NULL'; if off, as '0'. Affects emission output only, not internal analysis.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionIntegerFormat
intervention_surfaces.description: Set default integer constant display format (decimal, hexadecimal, octal, binary). Applies globally unless per-Symbol override is set.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionNoCastPrinting
intervention_surfaces.description: If enabled, suppresses explicit cast operators in output. Affects only emission, not internal type inference.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionAnalyzeForLoops (analyzeforloops)
intervention_surfaces.description: Controls whether to analyze and structure for-loops vs. emit as while-loops. Affects control-flow structuring output.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionJumpTableMax (jumptablemax)
intervention_surfaces.description: Sets upper limit on switch statement case count. If exceeded, switch recovery is skipped. Affects structuring.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionToggleRule
intervention_surfaces.description: Enable/disable individual Rule by name. Each rule can be toggled, affecting data-flow simplification pipeline. Allows user to control which transformations apply.
intervention_surfaces.affects: Any Rule in oppool1 or other rule pools

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionSetAction
intervention_surfaces.description: Switch between pre-configured action groups (e.g., 'decompile', 'jumptable', 'normalize'). Selects which transformations run at top level.

intervention_surfaces.name: Action Group Configuration (buildDefaultGroups)
intervention_surfaces.description: Pre-configured action group templates: 'decompile' (full), 'jumptable' (jump-table recovery), 'normalize' (proto normalization only), 'paramid', 'register', 'firstpass'. User can select via OptionSetAction.
intervention_surfaces.affects: Which actions execute in the top-level loop

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionExtraPop
intervention_surfaces.description: Override computed extra stack pop adjustment for unknown callees. Affects calling convention analysis and parameter recovery.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionDefaultPrototype
intervention_surfaces.description: Set the default prototype/calling convention to use when no symbol exists. Affects parameter/return type inference.

intervention_surfaces.name: OptionProtoEval
intervention_surfaces.description: Control how prototypes are evaluated (e.g., early vs. late binding, strict vs. permissive matching). Affects signature recovery.

intervention_surfaces.name: Symbol Database (Scope & Symbol classes)
intervention_surfaces.description: Core user-editable store for function/variable metadata. Symbols can have: name (user-assigned), data-type (locked or unlocked), storage location (address-tied), display format, category (parameter, equate, etc.). Persists across decompilations.
intervention_surfaces.affects: ActionNameVars naming, ActionInferTypes type propagation, all downstream analysis

intervention_surfaces.name: DynamicHash Symbol Attachment
intervention_surfaces.description: User can attach a Symbol to a temporary/ephemeral varnode by storing its dynamic hash (computed from local data-flow context). Used for union field selection and nickname assignment to temporaries.
intervention_surfaces.affects: Type interpretation and variable naming of temp values

intervention_surfaces.name: Per-Function Action Reset (clearAnalysis)
intervention_surfaces.description: When restart is triggered, ActionRestartGroup calls data.getArch()->clearAnalysis(), purging cached analysis data (types, covers, symbols) to allow re-computation with new constraints. User indirectly triggers via symbol edit.

insights: The Ghidra decompiler is NOT a linear pipeline but rather a complex feedback system. The key metaphor is 'edit state, then rerun everything': user edits to the Symbol database (type locks, name locks, overrides) are persisted, then the entire action pipeline is re-invoked from ActionStart. This is fundamentally different from most compilers, which assume one-way flow. The database is the ground truth.

Type inference operates via a fixed-point iterative propagation algorithm (7-pass limit) that is bidirectional within the 7 iterations. Each iteration runs propagateTypeEdge() across all varnodes, which consults per-opcode TypeOp rules. The restart flag (set by writeBack when types change) triggers re-execution of all downstream actions, including variable merging and naming. This is a 'whiteboard erase' restart: clearAnalysis() purges cached type/cover/symbol state before re-running.

Variable formation (merging) is distinct from variable naming and has two phases: (1) forced merges (phi-driven) during merging actions, and (2) speculative merges (heuristic-based, can be disabled per-symbol). Once merged, a HighVariable's cover and type are lazily recomputed via dirty flags. Speculative merges can be undone if user marks 'isolate' on a symbol, forcing a re-split on next run.

Explicit vs. Implied marking directly controls output readability. A varnode marked 'implied' is inlined into parent expressions; 'explicit' gets its own name/token. This is decided once by ActionMarkExplicit/ActionMarkImplied heuristics and does NOT interact with user intervention directly, but multiple merges can affect whether a variable qualifies as implicit (due to changed usage patterns).

Control-flow structuring via CollapseStructure is greedy and order-dependent: rules are tried in hard-coded priority (Goto, Cat, If, While, Switch, etc.). The first matching rule applies; then the graph is re-evaluated. Unstructured edges marked as gotos via TraceDAG heuristics. Unlike data-flow, structuring does NOT have a 'restart' loop visible to the framework; instead, it's a single pass with internal iteration. If structuring fails (edges remain), they become gotos.

The intervention model is coarse-grained: (1) type lock/name lock/isolation flags on Symbols prevent changes to those attributes, (2) dynamic symbol facets (UnionFacetSymbol) pinpoint specific union-field interpretations at code addresses, (3) action group and rule toggles control which transformations run. No mid-pass intervention is exposed; the user must edit and re-decompile.

Type locks are HARD constraints: propagateTypeEdge() immediately returns false if a varnode has typelock=true. This blocks bidirectional type flow. In contrast, name locks only affect naming, not typing. This asymmetry is intentional: type is semantic (affects correctness of generated code), name is cosmetic.

The pass limit of 7 for type inference is empirically determined, not derived from theory. It reflects a trade-off: enough iterations to converge on most functions, but not so many that performance suffers or rare non-terminating cycles trap the decompiler. Exceeding 7 passes triggers a warning, alerting the user to suspicious circular type dependencies.

Union field resolution via ScoreUnionFields is one of the few places where user annotation (UnionFacetSymbol) can directly override algorithmic choice. The user's annotation is consulted first; if it matches, that field is locked in. This is a 'trust the user' stance for complex type disambiguation.

The decompiler's handling of dynamic symbols (temporaries with per-location names/types) via DynamicHash is critical for readability: it allows 'renaming' a temporary register's value at different code points without creating separate HighVariables. A single temp varnode can have different symbol facets at different reads, depending on DynamicHash lookup.

Restart semantics are strictly scoped: only ActionRestartGroup (the outermost wrapper) checks restartPending. Inner loops (rule pools, rule application) have no restart logic. This means a restart request inside mainloop causes mainloop to fully rewind and re-execute, but does NOT restart earlier phases (like ActionPrototypeTypes). This prevents infinite outer loops while allowing inner convergence.
